chunks: And by his chain, he said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) went out while he was riding, so they walked along with him. He said to them: 'Is there any need for you?' They said: 'No, but we love to walk with you.' He said to them: 'Disperse, for the walking of the walker with the rider is a spoil for the rider and a humiliation for the walker.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette regarding walking with a rider according to Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the etiquette of public processions, noting that while walking beside a rider is an act of love, it inadvertently diminishes the rider's focus and dignity while imposing a subtle humiliation on the walker. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the preservation of hierarchical respect during public appearances, ensuring that gestures of affection do not compromise the leader's authority or the followers' status.
